# Blue block is in initial position. But I clicked the blue shape once earlier, which moved the green dots.
# Let me click on the blue shape again to see what happens.

# First, find the blue shape on the right side
ascii_lines = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
blue_shape_pixels = []
for r in range(14, 60):
    for c in range(32, 64):
        if ascii_lines[r][c] == 'b':
            blue_shape_pixels.append((r, c))
print(f"Blue shape pixels: {blue_shape_pixels[:20]}")

# Click on the blue shape (center of the shape)
if blue_shape_pixels:
    center_r = sum(r for r, c in blue_shape_pixels) // len(blue_shape_pixels)
    center_c = sum(c for r, c in blue_shape_pixels) // len(blue_shape_pixels)
    print(f"Clicking blue shape at ({center_r}, {center_c})")
    result = action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': center_r, 'col': center_c}])
    
    # Check what changed
    before_ascii = last_transition.before_frame.ascii.split('\n')
    after_ascii = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
    changes = []
    for r in range(60):
        for c in range(64):
            if before_ascii[r][c] != after_ascii[r][c]:
                changes.append((r, c, before_ascii[r][c], after_ascii[r][c]))
    gameplay_changes = [c for c in changes if c[0] < 60]
    print(f"\nAfter clicking blue shape: {len(gameplay_changes)} gameplay changes")
    for r, c, old, new in gameplay_changes[:30]:
        print(f"  ({r},{c}): {old} -> {new}")
    print(f"Level completed: {last_action_result.get('level_completed', False)}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
